consensus_summary: The phrase primarily denotes the four living creatures of the Ezekiel and Revelation throne visions, identified as cherubim-class angelic attendants who worship God and often symbolize the whole of animate creation (or, in long Christian tradition, the four Evangelists); a secondary lexical sense simply means any animate being.
book_summary: A nation or organized people, understood as the living counterpart of a beast or animal.
consensus_core_identification: Cherubim / exalted throne-attendant living creatures (Ezekiel–Revelation) or, secondarily, animate beings in general.
book_core_identification: Nation or organized people (living counterpart of a beast).
boundary_disagreement: None; the book’s referent is simply absent from the consensus range rather than a narrowed or re-bounded version of it.
material_contradiction: None; the identifications address different referents and do not directly negate each other.
rationale: Consensus responses uniformly center on the visionary cherubim of Ezekiel/Revelation (plus the ordinary Genesis sense of animate life) and list only Evangelist, Christological, creation-order, and astral alternatives. The book’s national/political reading appears in none of the primary or alternative meanings, so the relationship is pure novelty rather than refinement or contradiction of a shared core.
strongest_objection: The supplied texts either identify beasts (not living creatures) as kings or describe literal sea creatures dying; they do not establish the claimed national symbolism for “living creature.”
